content.title: Ex-MLB Player Daniel Serafini Murdered His Father-in-Law and Shot His Mother-in-Law. Here's Why He Did It
content.text: Daniel Serafini of the Minnesota Twins on March 1, 1999; Gary Spohr and Wendy Wood. Credit : Brian Bahr /Allsport via Getty; Placer County Sheriff's Office NEED TO KNOW In July 2025, ex-MLB player Daniel Serafini was found guilty of murdering his father-in-lawSerafini also attempted to kill his mother-in-law, who survived but died by suicide two years laterOn April 17, NBC's Dateline is airing the former baseball player's first sit-down interview from prison Daniel Serafini spent over two decades as a Major League Baseball player, but his life took a turn when he was found guilty of murder years later. The ex-MLB player played for the Minnesota Twins and Chicago Cubs in the late '90s. After his baseball career wound down, he met Erin Spohr when she was hired to work for his first wife to train their horses in 2006. Years later, and after Erin learned he was getting divorced, the pair began dating, got married and welcomed two children together, she shared during testimony later. Over the course of their marriage, Erin and Serafini had a tumultuous relationship with her parents, who were wealthy real estate investors and with whom they often fought over money and politics. Things took a turn in June 2021, when Erin's parents — Robert Gary Spohr and Wendy Wood — were shot in their $3.5 million Lake Tahoe, Calif., home. After a nearly two-year investigation, Serafini was arrested in October 2023 in connection with Gary's murder and the attempted murder of Wendy, who survived but died by suicide in 2023. He was found guilty in July 2025. Now, NBC's Dateline is revisiting Serafini's case in a new episode on April 17, which also saw the convicted killer give his first sit-down interview from prison. So, why did Daniel Serafini shoot his in-laws? Here's everything to know about the ex-MLB player's crimes. Serafini shot his in-laws in June 2021 Gary Spohr and Wendy Wood. Placer County Sheriff's Office On June 5, 2021, Gary and Wendy went out for a boat ride with Erin and her two young sons while they were visiting Lake Tahoe. While they were gone, Serafini snuck into their residence, where he would hide for approximately five hours, prosecutors said during the trial. After Erin and her sons left the home, Serafini emerged and shot Gary and Wendy. During the trial, prosecutors said that Serafini — who lost the millions that he earned in the major leagues on bad investments — attempted to kill his in-laws because he believed he would profit from their deaths. Prosecutors alleged he thought he would obtain his wife's $23 million inheritance. (Wood, however, later disinherited Erin.) Gary died on the scene, but Wendy was saved by paramedics Daniel Serafini, Wendy Wood, Gary Spohr and Erin Spohr. Courtesy Adrienne Spohr Gary died from a single gunshot to the head, though his wife survived after being shot twice in the head and once in the shoulder. Over the next two years, Wood spent much of her time undergoing intensive physical therapy and rehabilitation, relearning how to walk, talk, eat and perform other daily tasks. In February 2023, nearly two years after the shooting, she died by suicide. "The heartbreak of losing my dad — and knowing who was responsible [for his death] — became too much," Gary and Wendy's daughter, Adrienne Spohr, told PEOPLE in August 2025. "She said it felt like she had lost her right arm." Serafini and his mistress were arrested two years later Daniel Serafini; Samantha Scott. Placer County Sheriffs Office/Facebook Nearly two years after the shooting, Serafini was arrested in October 2023, alongside Samantha Scott, an occasional babysitter for his children. Scott was also his mistress and became his accomplice when she dropped him off at his in-laws on the day of the shooting. A few days later, Serafini's sister-in-law, Adrienne, released a full statement that was shared on X by NBC's Pete Suratos, reading, "The Call I received on October 20, 2023 will forever be etched in my mind - a moment of profound relief and gratitude after two years of fear and uncertainty. I feel an immense weight lifted off my shoulders." She added, "I have held onto my parents' ashes as I never felt right scattering them without the justice they deserved. Now that justice has been served, my parents can finally rest in peace." Serafini and his mistress' arrests came after Scott's cell phone data placed her near the scene of the crime. Scott struck a plea deal with prosecutors in which she would receive a lesser accessory charge in return for testifying against Serafini. Related Stories At the trial, Scott said that she drove Serafini to and from Lake Tahoe on the day of the incident and that she watched him fire a gun to test the plastic-pipe silencer he planned to use. Scott also claimed that she believed Serafini was traveling to Lake Tahoe to purchase a large quantity of cocaine on the day of the shooting. She alleged that at a later point, he confessed to shooting Wendy, but threatened to kill her if she told anyone. Following Scott's guilty plea, she was sentenced to two years of probation. Serafini was found guilty and sentenced to two terms of life in prison Daniel Serafini after he was found guilty of murder, attempted murder and burglary on July 14, 2025, in California. Paul Kitagaki Jr/TNS via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock In July 2025, Serafini was found guilty of first-degree murder and attempted murder of his in-laws, the Placer County District Attorney's Office confirmed in a press release shared on Facebook. The release also noted that he was additionally found guilty of "first-degree burglary and found the special circumstance allegations of lying-in-wait and felony murder, as well as related firearm allegations, to be true." In February 2026, Serafini was sentenced to two terms of life in prison without the possibility of parole, and also received 25 years to life on the third count of burglary. The judge ordered that all three sentences be served consecutively. "He is a monster who knows no moral boundaries and has zero reservations about taking the lives of others to benefit himself," Adrienne said at his sentencing hearing.
